facts.fact: COBAC's 2025 annual report, as reported 2026-10-09, covers payment institutions (non-bank) licensed in the CEMAC, and names Mobile Money Congo SA and Mobile Commerce Congo SA as the payment institutions operating in Congo, whose revenues rose 28.1% to FCFA 20.6 billion in 2025.

systems.tiers: banks, microfinance institutions, payment institutions and mobile money operators, aggregators, BEAC, Treasuries

note: Describes the GIMACPAY regional switch, its participants (16 payment institutions and mobile money operators among 153) and 2025 volumes; states no law, rule, licensing basis or obligation to connect.

facts.fact: ARTF, Congo's money-transfer regulator, said it will enforce from January 2027 the finance law's obligation on every money-transfer and exchange operator to register on its digital platform and use electronic payment terminals; the law is called 'en vigueur', and the article gives no year for the finance law.

systems.system: ARTF digital platform and electronic payment terminals (TPE)
systems.country_label: plateforme digitale de l'ARTF; terminaux de paiement électronique
systems.owner: ARTF (Agence de régulation des transferts de fonds)

note: A money-transfer registration and tax-capture rule, not e-money or payment-provider licensing; no non-bank licence and no provider-to-provider connection rule is stated.

facts.fact: ARTF's director said on 5 October 2026 that article 13 of the 2026 finance law obliges money-transfer operators to register on ARTF's digital platform and declare all transfers by the 10th of the following month, with a fine of 20 million FCFA for refusing to interconnect to the ARTF platform.

systems.owner: ARTF (Agence de régulation des transferts de fonds)

note: The interconnection duty is to the regulator's reporting platform, not between payment providers or to a payment switch, so no reach fact.

systems.tiers: public administrations and taxpayers; paid through commercial banks

note: Arrete 1009 of 22 May 2026 makes public-revenue payment through the FOUTA national switch compulsory; it is not a payments or e-money law and states no licensing or provider connection rule.

facts.fact: The Congolese finance ministry's arretes of 20 June 2025 cite CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC Regulation No. 04/18 of 21 December 2018 on payment services as the governing text for payment institutions.
Arrete No. 2708/MFBPP-CAB of 27 May 2022 approved Mobile Money Congo S.a as a payment institution (etablissement de paiement), per the Journal officiel of 3 July 2025.
